Definition: Chiram or Chirom, the name of two Tyrians
BiblicalUsage: Hiram is the name of two Tyrians, a king and a craftsman, and the books keep them distinct. Hiram king of Tyre sends his servants to Solomon and supplies timber for the temple, while Hiram the craftsman comes out of Tyre to cast the bronze work and finishes all the work for the house of the Lord.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe the two Hirams show how God uses both a king's friendship and a craftsman's hands to build His house. I hold that the craftsman's Hiram is the one I love most, because his work is still standing in the record.
RelatedPeople: Hiram, King of Tyre; Hiram, Craftsman of Tyre
